subject.title: Add Teams delegated auth for plugin tools

question: Should OpenClaw expose a generic execution-scoped plugin API that can release a Teams user’s raw delegated bearer token to explicitly authorized installed plugins?
rationale: The code can enforce a default-deny policy, but it cannot decide whether installed plugin code should ever receive this credential class or what permanent SDK and operator contract is acceptable.

options.title: Approve the delegated-token capability
options.body: Sponsor the generic default-deny API, then require a current-main rebase, dependency approval, and live Teams proof before merge.

options.title: Keep Teams auth channel-owned
options.body: Do not expose raw user tokens to plugin tools; instead keep token use inside a narrowly owned Teams or downstream integration surface.

options.title: Defer the API direction
options.body: Pause this PR until the plugin credential capability and policy model have an explicit maintainer design decision.

recommendation.title: Approve the delegated-token capability
recommendation.body: Sponsor the generic default-deny API, then require a current-main rebase, dependency approval, and live Teams proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged Teams SDK work owns the relevant sign-in and consent integration boundary that this generic plugin capability builds upon.
